case.case_title: Gamini Dissanayake v. M. C. M. Kaleel and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. (Special) No. 4-11/91, decided on 3 December 1991

clause.text: Any accused person has the right to a fair trial and legal representation.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners were denied their right to a fair trial or hearing in the disciplinary proceedings leading to their expulsion from the party.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed they were not given a fair hearing or opportunity to defend themselves before expulsion, violating their constitutional right to a fair trial.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the disciplinary process was valid and that the petitioners' rights were not materially affected as the Supreme Court proceedings constituted the right to an antecedent hearing.
key_facts: Petitioners were expelled without prior notice or hearing.
The disciplinary process was conducted by the Party's Working Committee.
Petitioners challenged the expulsions under Article 99 (13)(a) of the Constitution.
The Supreme Court heard the petitions and considered the fairness of the disciplinary process.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court emphasized that the right to a fair trial includes the right to be heard before any disciplinary action is taken. The disciplinary power of the party is subject to natural justice, requiring notice and opportunity to respond.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioners were not given notice of the charges or a chance to explain before expulsion. The court rejected the argument that subsequent Supreme Court proceedings cured this defect, holding that the lack of an antecedent hearing violated their right to a fair trial.
principles_established: Right to a fair trial includes prior notice and hearing in disciplinary matters.
Subsequent judicial review does not substitute for a fair initial hearing.
Disciplinary powers must be exercised fairly and in accordance with natural justice.
precedents_cited: General Medical Council v. Spackman [1943] AC 627
Joseph Perera v. A G. SC 107-109/86

outcome.holding: The expulsion of the petitioners was invalid due to denial of their right to a fair hearing, violating Article 13(3).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The expulsions are set aside; petitioners may face fresh disciplinary proceedings with proper hearing.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(3) guarantees the right to a fair trial, which the court found was denied in the disciplinary expulsion process due to lack of notice and opportunity to be heard, making this clause central to the court's reasoning and decision.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioners were neither informed of the allegations nor afforded an opportunity to submit an explanation or to be heard in their defence before expulsion, violating the audi alteram partem rule.
